findings.failure_trigger: Cell 3 generates six prefix/suffix variants of each of only 40 original descriptions, then cell 4 splits individual rows. findings.title: Validation/test split is unused in reported evaluation
findings.snippet:
validation_data, test_data = train_test_split(
    golden_data,
    test_size=0.50,
    random_state=42,
    stratify=golden_data["true_code"]
)
...
mrr = mean_reciprocal_rank(golden_data)
findings.failure_trigger: Normal execution: every downstream recall, comparison, MRR and JSON report evaluates golden_data, never validation_data or test_data.
findings.impact: The final metrics pool validation and held-out examples; the added split provides no independent test estimate. If validation is used for selecting weights/thresholds later, reported metrics will include tuned-on examples.
findings.fix: Use validation_data for comparisons/tuning, freeze settings, then compute and label final test metrics exclusively on test_data; export split membership.
findings.classification: actual evaluation wiring defect; tuning leakage is conditional, not demonstrated

findings.title: Failure-rate metric ignores invalid model responses
findings.failure_trigger: A substituted model returns None, an empty string, an unrecognized label or a misspelled/case-variant label rather than the two exact sentinels.
findings.impact: Invalid outputs are scored incorrect for accuracy but counted as successful responses in failure_rate. For example one invalid response in 30 cases yields 0% reported failure instead of 3.33%; two invalid responses violate the configured 5% threshold while failure_rate still reports zero. Other quality gates might independently block, but the failure gate itself is wrong.
findings.fix: Validate/normalize prediction against the allowed label set immediately after model invocation, classify all invalid outputs as failures, and retain raw outputs/errors for diagnosis.

findings.title: Confusion matrix omits failed predictions
findings.failure_trigger: Any model returns UNKNOWN or ERROR (both supported by evaluate_model), or any label outside LABELS.
findings.impact: Explicit labels excludes the extra prediction columns, dropping those observations from the displayed matrix; matrix row totals no longer match evaluation support and visually conceal failures. The supplied candidate may have no such failures, so this is a supported-path defect rather than a claimed current execution failure.
findings.fix: Include UNKNOWN, ERROR and all observed prediction labels in the matrix, or separately display failure counts and verify displayed totals equal the evaluation set.

findings.title: Deployment gate fails open on nonfinite metrics

findings.impact: Every ordered comparison with NaN is false, leaving reasons empty and returning PASS. Confirmed with stdlib-only extraction of the exact deployment_gate function and a minimal class-results stub: decision PASS, all reported changes NaN.
findings.fix: Before threshold comparisons, reject missing/nonfinite/out-of-range baseline/candidate metrics, empty class results and nonfinite class changes; return an explicit INVALID_EVALUATION failure.

findings.title: Split synthetic text by template before reporting generalization metrics
findings.snippet:
train_data, temp_data = train_test_split(
    data,
    test_size=0.40,
    random_state=RANDOM_STATE,
    stratify=data["document_type"]
)
findings.failure_trigger: Using validation_accuracy/test_accuracy as evidence of generalization to new enterprise documents. Cell 2 randomly repeats only eight templates per class and cell 3 splits rows rather than template groups; the RESUME class generates 100 rows from eight constant strings with no substitutions. Repeated template families can enter every split.
findings.evidence: AST inspection confirms all eight RESUME strings contain no formatting placeholders, so its 100 rows necessarily include at least 92 duplicate occurrences. Neither split groups by source template nor deduplicates text; vectorizer fitting itself correctly occurs only on train_data.
findings.suggested_fix: Track template_id during generation and group-disjoint split templates; also assert that normalized text and template IDs do not overlap across partitions. For enterprise generalization claims, evaluate on independently collected documents.
findings.checked_limits: Did not recreate NumPy/sklearn seeded generation or splitting; exact train/test duplicate count is unmeasured. This does not establish a fresh accuracy value or prove all test rows are duplicates.
findings.fix: Track template_id during generation and group-disjoint split templates; also assert that normalized text and template IDs do not overlap across partitions. For enterprise generalization claims, evaluate on independently collected documents.

findings.title: Successful JEV calls do not return a usable routing decision
findings.failure_trigger: Calling route_document(row, use_jev=True) for any row passing hard_policy, when ask_jev succeeds. Every successful response returns JEV_RESPONSE instead of one of AUTO_PROCESS/HUMAN_REVIEW/ESCALATE, regardless of the service answer.
findings.evidence: Stdlib reproduction extracted cells 12, 13, 19 and mocked ask_jev to return {"routing":"AUTO_PROCESS"}. Online result was {"decision":"JEV_RESPONSE","source":"jev","response":{"routing":"AUTO_PROCESS"}}, while the same row routed offline as AUTO_PROCESS. Cell 25 defines the three valid decisions but only checks offline inference_data.
findings.suggested_fix: Parse the documented JEV response schema, validate the selected route against the three allowed decisions, and return it in decision; use HUMAN_REVIEW for absent/invalid choices. Add a mocked online-path test.

findings.fix: Parse the documented JEV response schema, validate the selected route against the three allowed decisions, and return it in decision; use HUMAN_REVIEW for absent/invalid choices. Add a mocked online-path test.

findings.title: Rerunning experiment cell counts deterministic duplicates as independent observations
findings.failure_trigger: Rerun cell 19 without resetting cell 17, a normal interactive notebook action.
findings.impact: The same subject/query/variant is appended again with exactly the same deterministic correctness and latency. Aggregation reports twice as many requests and total cost; bootstrap resamples duplicate rows as independent subjects and can narrow uncertainty despite no new independent evidence.
findings.fix: Make a run explicit: reset logs at the start of cell 19, or assign run IDs and deduplicate by experiment/subject/request and bootstrap independent subject clusters.
